notes: Selected filters are readable again - the active state is now a calm neutral highlight instead of blue text on a blue fill, across the Inbox, Customers, Identity health and Conditional Access.

The Customers and Inbox lists read as a single table now, with the column header attached to its rows like Identity and Licenses. Inbox rows are calmer too: verdict tags (Auto-restored, Review sign-ins, GA) line up in their own column instead of crowding the title, the owner always shows a name rather than a raw id, and the description is trimmed so tenant, owner and age have room.

More squared-corner polish and faster triage: avatars and the resolved check-marks pick up the portal's squared corners, the Identity health summary cards are clickable (click Critical to filter to critical findings, worst first), the Licenses cards match the rest of the portal, and customer tenant IDs show a short head…tail you can click to copy the full id.

Every incident now tells its change story as a ledger on the affected policy: baseline, while the change was live, and now - with counts first (+ 5 excluded), names on demand, and the outcome stated outright (all removed - back at baseline). Readable in seconds even for big changes.
What-changed slims to the verdict and the raw diff - the story is told once, right next to the live state it explains. Timeline icons now match the portal's squared corners.

The incident page is redesigned: a calmer header with the owner shown by name (never a raw object-id), and Live policy state as a flat spec sheet - assignments collapse to clickable type counts and expand to a searchable list showing display names and sign-in addresses.
Small grey text across the portal is raised to a readable floor - sign-in addresses, owner names and customer tenant ids are no longer micro-print.
Audit attribution now records the operator's email even when the sign-in only carried a display name.
The 'update available' banner is calmer and gently animated, and the What's-new window is now a release timeline - every release since your version, newest first, with its change count.
Installing an update now shows real progress with an estimated time remaining instead of a plain spinner.

The Fleet overview is rebuilt: richer stat cards with honest trend badges, an alert-volume chart that stacks the four incident categories (Privilege escalation, Policy guard, Identity hygiene, Operations) from your real investigation log over the selected window, and an Open-cases table linking straight into each incident.
The whole portal now uses wide screens: the dashboard, Inbox, Customers, Identity health and Conditional Access pages widen to the same cap the incident page got - more data, fewer dead margins.
Status gets a face: open cases carry the new status pill (dashed circle = new, spinner = in progress, green check = resolved) - the first piece of the refreshed component language.
Tab strips across the portal hug their content again instead of stretching edge to edge - the compact form reads better on wide screens.

What's new now accumulates: skip a release and its notes carry into the next banner. The portal shows everything since YOUR running version, grouped per release - no more updates silently replacing the notes you never read.

The incident page uses big screens properly: evidence and impact cards take the extra width while the playbook and timeline keep their comfortable size - no more content squeezed between dead margins.
Quiet polish: tab count badges stay the same calm grey whether or not the tab is active - selection reads from the tab itself. Severity-tinted finding counts keep their red and amber.

The Basewiser B is now the browser tab icon - the brand mark on a card tile matching the portal design, crisp from pinned tabs up to full-size bookmarks. If your tab still shows the old icon, a hard refresh clears the cached one.

The inbox is rebuilt for triage: every incident is its own card with sortable columns (severity, tenant, owner, age), an incident category on each row (Privilege escalation, Policy guard, Identity hygiene, Operations), and a quick-actions menu - assign to me, take over, open the customer, copy the link - without opening the case.

Filters speak one language everywhere: multi-select pills with built-in search and one-click clear on the Inbox, Customers, Identity health and Conditional Access pages. Filter to two tenants and a category in three clicks; the X on the pill undoes it in one.

The Customers list gains search and sortable columns - sort by Alerts for the what's-on-fire view - and secondary tab rows across the portal are now full-width segmented strips, with the Identity tab reclaiming the space the old side table-of-contents held.

Role-grant alerts no longer reference an allowlist - there is no role allowlist; severity is purely tier-driven (GA above Tier 0, other roles lower). The change allowlist keeps governing guard-mode alerts, where it belongs.

Granter resolution is now three layers deep: the admin's own audit footprint resolves instantly, PIM schedule requests confirm intent (activation vs admin grant), and granter-less rows backfill for 24 hours - the WHO tile updates itself with a journal note.
Findings move with events: a role grant triggers the tenant's identity rescan immediately, and the active-alert badge updates the moment an incident is resolved.
